Name: Murder in a garage
Description:
A Murder in a Garage   A tragedy unfolded last night on the outer boulevard under circumstances not yet fully explained.   Yesterday evening, Mr. Florent Frauenberg-Pauls, a horse trader residing on Boulevard de la Foire, was at the establishment called "Vieux Luxembourg" in the company of a certain Mr. Armand Krier, a car driver residing in Luxembourg.   Shortly after them, there also arrived the named Dominique Kersch, 24 years old, a mechanic in Esch-sur-Alzette (mistyped as Aix-sur-Alzette), and two of his friends who had accompanied him on a sidecar ride.   A brief altercation occurred at one point between the companions of Kersch and Frauenberg. However, the argument did not last. Around 12:15 AM, as they were preparing to leave, Kersch told Frauenberg and Krier that a rather serious breakdown had occurred with his sidecar. The latter examined it, and finally Frauenberg proposed to carry out the necessary repairs at the former Wag- garage located on Boulevard Extérieur, currently operated by Messrs. Hoffmann and Pauls, the latter being Frauenberg's brother-in-law.
From the moment the men entered the garage, a bit of mystery—which, moreover, would soon be dispelled—shrouded the tragedy. According to the information obtained at the present time, just as the repair was about to be completed and Kersch was still bent over the machine, he received a formidable blow to the back of his neck delivered with a club or a hammer. Kersch stated that he managed to straighten up and wanted to defend himself against Frauenberg, who fled. Kersch then had time to grab his revolver; he fired and Frauenberg fell struck dead.
Meanwhile, Krier had hidden behind an automobile, but Kersch, threatening him with his revolver, forced him to come out of his hiding place, enter the office, and keep his hands in the air. Once there, Kersch telephoned the police to report that he was being attacked by bandits and that he had killed a man. Then he waited, continuing to aim his revolver at Krier, who remained in the same position.
It was in this situation that Commissioner Entringer and his officers found the two men. It was then two o'clock in the morning.
At the time of writing, the Public Prosecutor's Office is carrying out the usual investigations, and the results will no doubt soon be known, along with the conclusions of the forensic doctor in charge of the autopsy.
Frauenberg, born July 7, 1890, married since 1914, was the father of a young daughter.
